countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

courses.name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy
courses.summary: Bachelor of Physiotherapy is the Students Traffic catalogue category for undergraduate-entry physiotherapy degrees. In India the BPT normally runs four academic years followed by a one-year clinical internship, is entered from a school-leaving qualification with physics, chemistry and biology, and covers anatomy, exercise therapy, electrotherapy and physiotherapy in musculoskeletal, neurological and cardiothoracic conditions with supervised hospital practice.

courses.name: Bachelor's in Occupational Therapy
courses.summary: Bachelor's in Occupational Therapy is the Students Traffic catalogue category for undergraduate degrees that train therapists to restore daily function after injury, illness or disability. Indian BOT degrees typically combine four academic years of anatomy, physiology, psychology, biomechanics and occupational therapy practice in medical, neurological, psychiatric and paediatric conditions with a one-year compulsory rotatory internship.

courses.name: Bachelor's in Psychology
courses.summary: Bachelor's in Psychology is the Students Traffic catalogue category for undergraduate degrees in psychology, including applied psychology programmes. Three-year Indian B.Sc. and B.A. programmes usually cover cognitive, developmental, social, clinical and counselling psychology, research methods and statistics, with practical assessment work and observation postings, and lead to postgraduate study in clinical, counselling or organisational psychology.

courses.name: Master of Public Health
courses.summary: Master of Public Health is the Students Traffic catalogue category for postgraduate degrees in population health. Programmes are normally open to graduates of medicine, dentistry, nursing, allied health, life sciences and several non-clinical disciplines, and teach epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy and management, environmental and occupational health and health promotion, with a field practicum and dissertation.

courses.name: Master's in Clinical Psychology
courses.summary: Master's in Clinical Psychology is the Students Traffic catalogue category for postgraduate degrees focused on psychological assessment, psychopathology and therapy. Two-year M.Sc. or M.A. programmes normally require a psychology bachelor's degree and combine theory with supervised clinical rotations and a dissertation; in some countries, including India, independent practice as a clinical psychologist needs a further regulated qualification.

courses.name: MBA in Healthcare Management
courses.summary: MBA in Healthcare Management is the Students Traffic catalogue category for management master's degrees specialised in hospitals and health systems. Programmes combine core management subjects such as finance, marketing, HR and analytics with hospital operations, healthcare quality and accreditation, health insurance and clinical governance, and usually include hospital postings, a summer internship and a dissertation.

universities.name: Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research
universities.summary: Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research (SRIHER) is a private deemed-to-be university on a 150-acre campus at Porur, Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Its 15 constituent faculties span medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, nursing, physiotherapy, allied health, public health, psychology, management and engineering around a teaching hospital on the same campus. Foreign nationals and NRIs apply through its International Relations Office.
universities.campusLifestyle: The 150-acre Porur campus holds 15 constituent faculties, a teaching hospital the university reports at more than 2,500 beds, a 40,000 sq ft central library open 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. on working days, a swimming pool, playgrounds, a bank with ATMs, a post office, a railway reservation counter and multi-cuisine restaurants. Student life runs through 16 clubs including dance, debate, fitness, Rotaract, Tamil, English literature, theatre and yoga, six NSS units, and Army and Naval NCC wings. SRIHER reports an alumni network of more than 20,000 graduates.
universities.cityProfile: SRIHER is at Porur in western Chennai, the capital of Tamil Nadu on India's south-east coast, with the postal address Porur, Chennai 600 116. The campus works as a self-contained township with colleges, staff quarters, a medical centre, the university hospital, retail stores and a travel service, so most day-to-day needs are met on site. Foreign nationals complete Foreigners Regional Registration Office formalities in Chennai after admission, with the university filing the residence and student registrations. First-year teaching starts in July: for 2026-27 entrants, undergraduate classes were scheduled to begin around the second week of July and postgraduate classes around the third week, with exact dates emailed to admitted students in advance.
universities.practicalExposure: Clinical and field training is built around Sri Ramachandra Hospital, a tertiary care and referral centre inside the campus that the university reports sees an average of 5,000 out-patients a day. The Bachelor of Physiotherapy is offered under the NCAHP allied and healthcare professions framework, with fourth-year clinical rotations and a one-year internship across musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiology and ICU, pulmonology, sports, obstetric, paediatric, oncology and burns physiotherapy. The Bachelor of Occupational Therapy includes supervised clinical training or field work in every academic year before a one-year compulsory rotatory internship. The M.Sc. Clinical Psychology includes two clinical rotations, psychological assessment practicals and a dissertation. The Master of Public Health is run by the Faculty of Public Health, whose Department of Environmental Health Engineering has been a WHO Collaborating Centre for occupational health since 2007 and started the MPH in collaboration with the University of California, Berkeley; students add a field practicum, a dissertation and an internship. The MBA in Hospital and Health Systems Management includes two hands-on hospital postings, a summer internship and a dissertation. SRIHER's placement cell reports about 700 offers through 230 campus processes in its latest cycle, with packages from INR 2.2 lakh to INR 72 lakh a year.
universities.hostelOverview: International students live in separate hostels for men and women inside the campus, with wardens assigned to international residents. For 2026-27 the published international hostel rates are USD 1,700 a year for an air-conditioned single room with common bath (USD 750 one-time caution deposit), USD 900 for an air-conditioned twin share or a non-air-conditioned single (USD 375 deposit each) and USD 450 for a non-air-conditioned twin share (USD 300 deposit). Fees are paid at admission and then annually, and rooms are allotted subject to availability. Hostel entry and exit are logged by biometric readers, entrances are under CCTV, and hostel gates close at 9 p.m.
universities.dietarySupport: Mess and canteen dining is provided inside the hostel complexes, and students pay the mess directly before hostel admission at the rate SRIHER notifies each year; this is not included in the hostel fee. Meals are served only in the mess, with no room service, and night cafeterias in the hostels sell snacks, coffee and tea between 9 p.m. and 1 a.m. Carbonated beverages and junk food are banned on university premises under a Government of India higher-education directive.
universities.safetyOverview: SRIHER applies the UGC, medical, dental and AICTE anti-ragging regulations and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act 1997, and reported no ragging incidents in the current year. Health insurance is mandatory for foreign students at USD 50 a year, and the campus hospital runs a 24-hour emergency service with an ambulance, treating students at concessional charges.
universities.studentSupport: The International Relations Office handles foreign-national and NRI admissions, pre-arrival guidance, FRRO registration, Bonafide Certificates and APAAR IDs for students without Aadhaar. Three student counsellors offer free, confidential sessions on the third floor of the IQAC wing, every student is assigned a faculty mentor, and an international student orientation is held on arrival.

The 2026-27 international prospectuses publish a total programme fee in US dollars for each listed degree, payable in two to four instalments, so the full tuition commitment is known before applying.

faq.question: Is Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research a public or a private university?
faq.answer: SRIHER is a private, not-for-profit, self-financing institution. It began in 1985 as Sri Ramachandra Medical College and Research Institute, set up by the Sri Ramachandra Educational and Health Trust, was declared a Deemed to be University by the Government of India in September 1994 under Section 3 of the UGC Act, and took its current name in August 2018. It is not a state or central government university.

faq.question: Who can apply to SRIHER as an international student?
faq.answer: The Foreign National category covers holders of a foreign passport, including OCI cardholders, and Nepal or Bhutan citizens holding citizenship cards. For postgraduate programmes OCI cardholders may apply only as foreign nationals. Non-Resident Indians and NRI-sponsored candidates use a separate NRI category with its own application and fee table. Applications filed in the wrong category are not considered.

faq.question: Do international applicants sit an entrance examination?
faq.answer: Foreign nationals and NRIs are exempt from SRIHER's own undergraduate and postgraduate entrance examinations for programmes governed by university regulations, unless a programme specifies otherwise, and are admitted on first-cum-first-served merit; SRIHER may hold an online interview. Programmes governed by councils follow those councils' rules, and the 2026-27 application states that admission to NCAHP programmes requiring NEET cannot be confirmed without a valid NEET appearance.

faq.question: What language are SRIHER programmes taught in, and is IELTS or TOEFL required?
faq.answer: SRIHER's programme regulations make English the medium of instruction and examination. The 2026-27 international prospectuses do not list an IELTS or TOEFL requirement; English is assessed through the qualifying examination instead, for example English at AS Level or five IGCSE or GCSE passes including English for A Level applicants, and English as a subject for IB applicants.

faq.question: Can I apply with A Levels or the International Baccalaureate?
faq.answer: Yes, for programmes where SRIHER publishes those routes. For B.Sc. Applied Psychology, A Level applicants need three Science or three Arts subjects at A Level, five IGCSE or GCSE passes including English and an average of grade D; IB applicants need a Diploma or Certificate with three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects, 24 points overall and at least 3 in each subject. All foreign school qualifications also need a UGC equivalence certificate.

faq.question: How much does it cost to study at SRIHER as a foreign national?
faq.answer: SRIHER publishes a total programme fee in US dollars. For 2026-27 entrants examples are USD 26,500 for the five-year BPT or BOT, USD 14,000 for the three-year B.Sc. Applied Psychology, USD 7,000 for the two-year MPH and USD 9,500 for the M.Sc. Clinical Psychology. On top come a one-time USD 50 registration fee, USD 50 a year health insurance, university examination fees, hostel from USD 450 to USD 1,700 a year plus a one-time caution deposit, and mess charges.

faq.question: How do I apply to SRIHER from abroad?
faq.answer: Download the category-specific 2026-27 application from the SRIHER admissions page and email it with scanned documents to admissions.international@sriramachandra.edu.in; there is no application fee in the international category. The International Relations Office and Admissions Committee check eligibility, issue an Offer of Provisional Admission, and after the first instalment is paid and final results are submitted, issue the confirmation letter used for the student visa.

faq.question: When does the SRIHER intake start and when do applications close?
faq.answer: SRIHER admits international students once a year for a July start. For 2026-27 the last date for foreign-national undergraduate applications was 30 June 2026, with classes from around the second week of July, and the last date for NRI and foreign-national postgraduate applications was 10 July 2026, with classes from around the third week of July.

faq.question: What visa and registration steps apply to international students?
faq.answer: Foreign nationals need an Indian student visa, not a tourist visa, and those who need a visa are admitted only once it is issued. Postgraduate foreign-national applicants must register on the Study in India portal, obtain an SII ID and apply for the visa through it. SRIHER registers each foreign student and their campus residence with the FRRO within 24 hours of admission, and students on visas longer than 180 days register with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival.

faq.question: How is SRIHER accredited and ranked?
faq.answer: NAAC accredited SRIHER A++ with a CGPA of 3.53 in its third cycle, declared in January 2021. The National Board of Accreditation lists the B.Pharm at the Faculty of Pharmacy to 30 June 2028 and the MBA in Hospital and Health Management to 30 June 2027. In NIRF 2025 SRIHER ranked 21st for medical, 13th for dental, 36th for pharmacy and 60th among universities. Professional registration abroad is decided by each country's own licensing body.

faq.question: Where do international students live, and what does accommodation cost?
faq.answer: Separate on-campus hostels for men and women are reserved for international students. The 2026-27 annual rates are USD 1,700 for an air-conditioned single, USD 900 for an air-conditioned twin share or non-air-conditioned single, and USD 450 for a non-air-conditioned twin share, plus a one-time caution deposit of USD 300 to USD 750. Mess charges are paid separately, and rooms are allotted subject to availability.

faq.question: Can foreign nationals study MBBS or BDS at SRIHER?
faq.answer: Not through a published route in 2026-27. SRIHER's foreign-national undergraduate prospectus and application forms for 2026-27 are issued for programmes excluding medical and dental degrees, so MBBS and BDS do not appear among the programmes offered to foreign nationals this cycle. Allied-health, psychology, public-health and management degrees are the programmes with a published international route.

faq.question: What happens to fees if I withdraw from a programme?
faq.answer: SRIHER states that fees paid to the university are not refunded or adjusted. A student who discontinues after the admission cut-off date, or whose seat cannot be refilled, must pay tuition and other fees for the entire remaining programme period, and certificates such as the transfer certificate and mark sheets are withheld until that payment is made.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.
